# nova-sprint roadmap

<!-- Generated from docs/roadmap.sexp by tools/roadmap. Do not edit this file: edit docs/roadmap.sexp and run `make roadmap`. -->

This is the nova-sprint, nova-card and nova-work work after the point releases. The release plan (the owner, 2026-10-11) replaces the ladder of 2026-10-09. The v1.2.x point releases come first and are cut in turn: v1.2.10 (being cut), v1.2.11 small fixes, v1.2.12 tests and models only, v1.2.13 contraction (fewer lines, no behaviour change), v1.2.14 the next small fixes; FIXES.md holds each one's scope and fixes, and an item below whose target is a v1.2.x release is waiting for its card. The aim is v1.2.x working pretty well, so it is the reference for intended behaviour: v1.3, unstable, is the re-architecture (the client/server conversion, then each layer secured from the bottom), built by the sprint running on v1.2.x and checked against it, rather than a blind rewrite; like getting a compiler self-hosting, then using it to build a better compiler. v1.4 is the stable release of v1.3, architecturally correct top to bottom. Point releases continue until only architectural items are open: an area stops taking point fixes when a fix there is the same problem in another form, or would be its third, and each v1.3 architectural item names the point fixes it replaces. Friend work is dogfooded within the week, once more friends are online: friends alone, then friends and fleet together, each friend bug a point-release card. These items were the sprint half of nova-tools' roadmap and moved here with the split, with the sprint's docs and models; nova-tools' ROADMAP.md holds the rest. Point-release work is in FIXES.md, not here. Each item says what it is and why it waits. Where the code already has part of an item, the item says what exists and covers only the gap.

## Lessons from Prime Agent's rewrite

Prime Intellect's write-up of rewriting Prime Agent with AI workers (https://www.primeintellect.ai/blog/prime-agent-rust) names what made a large AI-built rewrite hold together. Each item is one of those lessons, checked against nova's code at dev 9ff68178: what already exists is named by file and line, and the item covers the rest.

### The verifier is its own system stage

A card's checks are written before the work starts. After the work, a verifier stage of the system runs them in a fresh bench, apart from the reader, and its verdict is the merge gate: the named test must fail at the card's base and pass at its head, run by the system rather than reported by the worker. This changes the card contract (the TEST line becomes a check the system runs), the lander (one red-at-base, green-at-head run per card before the batch gate) and the reader's job (it reads a change already shown to do what the card says).

Already in the code: The card lint requires the named test to be absent at the base: rule donewhen-test-name, internal/swarm/lintbase.go:198-236 and internal/swarm/lintpaths.go:174-192. The member's native gate runs failing tests at the base only to classify a failure the worker already reported as not done (cmd/nova-swarm/nativegate.go:26-42). The lander's tree gate runs the batch at its head and reads the TEST line only to time the package (internal/sprint/gate_wall.go:46-59). No step runs the named test red at base and green at head as a gate; that is the gap. The system gates before reads item, under the sprint system, holds the cards that started on it.

Why it waits: A new system stage, not a fix.

### The reader is a different model from the implementer

A reader catches more when it does not share the implementer's blind spots. The rule: a card's reads go to a model other than the one that did the work, with an adversarial brief (find what is wrong; do not summarize) and access to the repository at the card's head. This changes read dealing and the read brief, and adds the rule to SPEC-SPRINT.

Already in the code: nova-sprint set --read-tier and stream set --read-tier raise the tier reads draw from (cmd/nova-sprint/verbs.go:3375 and 3469), and a friend never reads her own work (internal/sprint/friend_read.go:333). Nothing requires a different model; that rule is the gap.

Why it waits: A new dealing rule, not a fix.

### Findings go back to the same implementer

A reader's findings go back to the worker that wrote the change, as a rework of the same card: never a new card, and never a fresh worker who has to learn the change again.

Already in the code: This is the rule for cards and friends today. A card is edited in place, never twinned, and a friend's rework comes back to her (ReworkPinned, internal/sprint/friend_deal.go:89-96). The gap is the fleet, where a machine card's rework can go to any member. That is card rework-goes-to-the-same-worker-b, held under the dealing policy item.

Why it waits: Mostly in place; the rest is a dealing policy change, listed once under the dealing policy item.

## The sprint system

New verbs, stages and policies for nova-sprint. Each is new capability, so none of it fits the fixes-only ladder.

### Processor layers 3 to 8

The upper layers of the nova-sprint processor design: cards that name operands outside the sprint, a route predictor run in shadow first, speculative dispatch, vector cards that make one change across many targets, and a spend governor.

Why it waits: New capability; no new features through v1.4.

Replaces 6 open sprint cards, each mapped to `processor-layers`.

### A merge tree for promotion

Promotion through a merge tree: a root, a shadow, and a switch between them; and a stream's batch built from its cards' branches. Its TLA+ model goes with it: the merge-tree half of card tla-merge-tree-promotion-b. The promotion half of that card models shipped code and stays in v1.4.

Why it waits: New capability.

Replaces 4 open sprint cards, each mapped to `merge-tree`.

### Dealing policy

Changes to how work is dealt: subscription-billed friends before paid API, fewer tokens per friend card, a rework back to the same worker on the fleet as well as for friends, shared paths worked in parallel, and deal latency measured and bounded.

Why it waits: A policy change, not a fix.

Replaces 5 open sprint cards, each mapped to `dealing-policy`.

### System gates before reads

Checks the system can make run before any reader is paid: a mechanical card is proved by the system and not read, and the work lint proves that a card's test pins its change. This is where the verifier stage, under the lessons, starts.

Why it waits: New capability.

Replaces 3 open sprint cards, each mapped to `machine-gates-before-reads`.

### Integrity checks (fsck)

Checks the seat or a person can run at any time: each friend's queue agrees with the store, nothing is held without a beat, every pushed head is recorded, the server's runs and pushes agree, and every landed card is on the base.

Why it waits: New verbs.

Replaces 5 open sprint cards, each mapped to `fsck-integrity-verbs`.

### Two new alarms

An alarm when the store's latency passes its bound, and one when a test process is left running on a fleet machine.

Why it waits: New capability.

Replaces 2 open sprint cards, each mapped to `new-alarms`.

### A spend circuit breaker with a budget per tier

Dealing to a tier stops when its spend passes the tier's budget, and says so.

Why it waits: New capability. The per-model request budget the owner named is v1.3 and separate.

Replaces 1 open sprint card, each mapped to `spend-circuit-breaker`.

### Retire the stopgaps once their verbs exist

Each stopgap goes when the verb that replaces it exists: the bud runners, buswatch, the ping and beat loops, the opencode runners, the coordinator's shell lanes, and the hand steps of promotion.

Why it waits: Each one waits on a new verb.

Replaces 7 open sprint cards, each mapped to `retire-stopgaps`.

### A verb to reland a card from its commits

A verb that lands a card again from named commits.

Why it waits: A new verb.

Replaces 1 open sprint card, each mapped to `reland-from-commits-verb`.

### A cost category for friend work, in tokens

Friend work counted in tokens as its own cost category beside the tiers, so subscription work shows its real size.

Why it waits: New capability.

Replaces 1 open sprint card, each mapped to `friends-token-cost-category`.

### The tree gate tells a bench fault from a red test

When a gate fails because of the bench rather than the code, the lander says so and does not charge the card for it.

Already in the code: Part of it is on dev (c5922306bf, 5d8e164a50); pull request 5476 carries more.

Why it waits: Parked by the owner, 2026-10-09.

Replaces 1 open sprint card, each mapped to `lander-bench-fault-classifier`.

### Refuse a need that names a dropped card, and list dependants on drop

Admission already refuses a need that names no record, but a dropped card is still a record. Add refuses a need on a card that can no longer land, and dropping a card lists the cards that need it.

Target: v1.5

### Convert every client-held copy of sprint state to client/server

The first v1.4 rewrite step. Each item in the 2026-10-10 inventory where a client keeps its own copy of sprint state is converted in place so the server is the one truth and clients ask it: the friend daemon's lanes and epoch, the member loop's lane table and local recovery (one lane protocol for friends and fleet), the seat's file proof, friend messages through folders and the separate bus Redis, config split across Postgres and the store, hosts following versions, the dashboard's own snapshot, and the lander as a second truth in git. All state is keyed by epoch. A TLA+ model of the lane protocol comes first. Faults found while the point releases run are recorded here as input.

Why it waits: Point releases continue meanwhile; their faults are the input to this rewrite cleanup.

Target: v1.5

From: the owner, 2026-10-11

### Secure the sprint's layers from the bottom up

Name the layers that are really there and secure each in turn, lowest first, each an anchor so a later fault stops there: L0 machine (one join entry point, drift check, doctor member-env green); L1 transport (loops re-dial, seat proof, push delivery); L2 providers and routes (the global limiter live, a provider fault never fails a card); L3 deal and take (a machine fault holds the machine, no silent ready); L4 read (no lost verdict, no cannot-ask while readers idle); L5 land (ledger merge done, judgments rare and hands-off); L6 observability (doctor and pushes catch every fault first). A layer is secured when it has a TLA+ model with reversed witnesses checked by TLC, tests on a real store including every refusal, a second reader's probes green, real use by the seat and by friends, docs, and a lock agreed with the owner.

Why it waits: Comes after the client/server conversion of the 2026-10-10 inventory, so the layers are secured on the converted design rather than on client-held state.

Target: v1.5

From: the owner, 2026-10-11

A launcher refusal before any process starts returns the card to the queue instead of raising it unknown. The queue remembers dealt labels and refuses a repeat unless forced.

From: issue #2381; issue #2382

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2386; issue #2530; issue #2508; issue #2407

A reader reverts the commit each new test claims to pin, expects red, restores it and expects green, and reports per test.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2387

### Each machine computes its sprint row and pushes it to a store

Every machine builds its own row of queue, working, done, ok, fail and rates every ten seconds, and the viewer reads the store.

Target: after v1.4

Self-contained cards need no repo, cards run only the useful test command with cached tool discovery, and Go parallelism is bounded per card.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2399; issue #2400; issue #2401

A finding on the current batch becomes a card at the front of the swarm and merge queue, keeping the fix close to the base.

From: issue #2417

CI carries the machine-checkable evidence and the PR body opens with title, goal, write scope and test command. Report and read start when the PR opens, and the reader sees only the diff and statuses.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2449; issue #2531; issue #2509

A typed approve line is counted, and an untyped hold can be released by a read.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #2454

Result and read files follow a schema parsed without a model. A finished result is cached by card text and base, and the base is pinned at deal time.

From: issue #2506; issue #2507; issue #2529

### Sprint table counts come from a card event stream, not file times or comment scans

Done, ok, fail, read, landed and calibration counts per friend and per bench are folded from card events, so the table needs no GitHub scan and shows cut to landed.

From: issue #2563; issue #2678; issue #2680

One reader loads the roadmap and work files, a landed acceptance kind exists, and a sprint is any bounded task set answering x/y percent in under a second, with GitHub issues ingested into the file.

The sprint verb records the start once, and bench counts read it, so counts never include an earlier sprint.

Each card gets a stable id carried to job, result, event and PR body, names its ruling and spec anchor, and one query answers why a PR exists, with its siblings and attempts.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2589; issue #2596; issue #2597

The sprint table and status print the items waiting on a human, such as asked cards, PRs with no typed line and held cards, with who is expected, and a supervisor owns the notifications.

From: issue #2592

The batch test step keeps the raw go test JSON stream, paginated review captures are not truncated at the output cap, and the gate's receipt is stored where a reader can fetch it.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #2626; issue #2654; issue #2693; issue #3183

A webhook receiver writes GitHub events to a stream with a durable consumer and a polling fallback, so PR, CI and typed-line changes reach loops and the table within seconds.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #2657; issue #2685

### Owner decisions are records with options, default, deadline and ruling

A decide verb opens, shows and rules decision records, and the table shows one count of open decisions.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3143

### nova-work ingest from GitHub: capture, continuous poll, verify and cutover

nova-work reads issues from GitHub into its own store with conditional requests, keeps in sync from deliveries and a poll, and has a verify run. The tracker becomes a mirror once the cutover is done.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3167; issue #3169; issue #3172; issue #3173; issue #2080; issue #2081; issue #2082

One writer applies roadmap batches back to the tracker, reports how far the mirror lags, and settles units when landed pull requests and verified criteria arrive.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3168; issue #3171

### nova-work keeps specs in its store behind a single-writer kernel

Specs, their versions and reader scores live in the nova-work store, and the ready gate is computed from them. One kernel owns the store and every mutating verb is a kernel command.

From: issue #3220; issue #3340

Queues, leases and tables live in the sprint store, not in files. Every store access is a pipelined batch, every loop ticks at one second, and coordination scripts move into Go verbs.

From: issue #3279; issue #3303; issue #3309

### Decisions are made centrally; machines only execute what the queue says

A worker machine takes the next ready item, runs it and reports. It never decides readiness from a partial view.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3251

Every coordinator action is a verb, and the loops and tables run on any Mac or Linux machine with failover, so no step depends on one person or host.

Target: after v1.4

The stop and its lift are set and cleared by a verb and held in the sprint store, so a friend never relies on a bus note to know whether to work.

Target: after v1.4

Cards, pull requests and issues state dependencies in one canonical form read by one parser. Unknown dependency state is never treated as satisfied.

Spec reads use one machine-checked line form written by a verb. A verb computes the gate verdict from the store, reads are keyed to the body hash so stale ones never count, and a rewrite names the gaps it closes.

From: issue #3564; issue #3565; issue #3566; issue #3568; issue #3569

A stream is opened, taken, batched, marked and landed as a unit, holding at its boundary. Cancelled or timed-out shards count as red.

From: issue #3478

The table shows each live child with task, step, age and cost, read from the store, including reads and spec reviews that hold no queue lease.

Target: after v1.4

Read-family cards carry a low turn limit and low reasoning, and writing-family cards a higher one, to cut tokens per card.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3534

### Sprint table: disk room per host and one consumer table for friends and hosts

The sprint table shows free disk per host, red under the floor, and one table shape (ready, working, done, ok, fail, ok%) for friends and hosts.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3584; issue #4071

### The card record is the only record; GitHub is a remote written at the edges

Cards carry their fields as structured data imported once at creation. Nothing parses prose or edits a pull request body, and GitHub is touched only to close out. A call budget guard counts remaining GitHub calls meanwhile.

Target: after v1.4

From: issue #3594; issue #3596; issue #3601; issue #3607; issue #3633; issue #3603; issue #3967

Reads live in one record with one writer, and a read counts only when the verb writes its score line. A score posted only on the bus cannot exist.

From: issue #3874; issue #3897; issue #2063

### Cards carry what changed on the base, and merge notes reach live workers

The card cut lists base commits touching its paths since the issue, and a note verb lets merge learnings reach a worker mid-task.

From: issue #4189; issue #4186

A waiting card is complete, so a deal is one move. Verbs deal, work, end, land and cancel are the only writers of stream, host and friend sets, and everything stays in the store under one second.

From: issue #3636; issue #3662; issue #3911; issue #3929

From: issue #3999; issue #4155; issue #4072

A card carries evidence, paths with lines, seams, rules, receipts and keep notes. Push refuses a work card missing them, and requires a stream.

A parent fans out from a plan, depends on its children, takes corrections mid-flight, then reviews and stitches in its second phase.

Target: after v1.4

### Dependencies come from paths, with sentinels per layer

Ready means no live path overlap. Streams follow the file graph, overlap is refused at push, and a sentinel card reviews each layer and across streams.

From: issue #4318; issue #4322; issue #4188; issue #4185; issue #4028

One spelling per concept, one receipt shape, fast quiet calls and a home screen. The system settles what it can before waking the coordinator.

A fresh coordinator seat gets a durable, supervised recipe that turns new judgments and notes into a wake for its harness. Delivery, wake and acknowledgement are separate steps.

Watchdog exit must not wait on diagnostics that can block. A negative deadline is refused.

Cheap tier first, pro only on escalation. Two identical failures escalate at once. A route that returns no result rests. Rules are kept by reference, each with a unit test.

Two cards that shrink the same ledger conflict by line. Regenerate the ledger at the merged tree, and stage rework from the current head.

A fix-red card kind names its source and test files and its reproducing test, and is accepted only when that test goes green. One card per triaged defect.

### nova-work client must stop waiting after a bound

A work client call without a deadline waits forever on a session that never answers. The spec fixes a default bound and the client enforces it.

Target: v1.5

From: issue #1643

### A card goes from issue to landed with no coordinator hand step

List what remains before accept, routing, reads and landing all run by the system alone, and close each gap.

Target: after v1.4

A coordinator learns what each friend can do now and whether workers share one account limit. Stale advertisements do not count.

Target: after v1.4

Authenticated control events with scope, update number and priority reach every running descendant, and the sprint can prove each one applied.

Target: after v1.4

The sprint persists the goal, gates, priorities and budget, and recovers from a failed worker, exhausted provider or lost context while the owner is away.

Target: after v1.4

A single dealer with per-member queues stops fast-ping machines from winning every card while slow ones sit idle.

Every remote call has a timeout and each host is isolated, so a dead machine and stale connection sockets cannot freeze the loops.

Provider capacity is a shared resource. Ceilings, an error-rate watch and automatic spill to the next route keep retries from holding slots.

Target: after v1.4

Widths are measured, not guessed, and limits are found by a controlled ramp.

Card generators become verbs that cut from a work spec, a repair or a read, and skip work an open or merged pull request already carries.

From: issue #2021; issue #2041; issue #2047

One signal with a generation is checked by dealing, launch, harvest and landing before each action, and bad signal states cause no side effect.

The first few cards of a new family run alone, and a machine is checked at loop start, so mass failures show in minutes.

Launched, returned, gate result, pull requests and landed are counted per wave and per model, with live cards and widths by machine, all from records.

Two members sharing a commit are not a conflict. The planner finds stacks by ancestry, not by base ref.

One verb collects returns, applies commits, runs the suite, opens the pull request and records each verdict on its source.

Expand a derive form to one node per matching issue and a fold form to one node over its green sibling branches, excluding non-green ones.

Hold an uncertain reservation and never re-grant it on expiry, reap on lease expiry, and give the executor seam a parent grant, a version-bound result and uncertain-on-disconnect.

From: a Gemini dialog the owner shared, 2026-10-10

### A TLA+ case for the false-positive fix loop

A fix passes its own layer but keeps re-failing a sentinel above it. A TLA+ case couples components to domains: a fix confined to PATHS that never meet the regression's component exhausts its attempt bound and halts. When widened PATHS intersect the component, the fix clears it nondeterministically (it may still fail), and every failure counts toward MaxAttempts: intersection is necessary, not sufficient. Properties: a reachable fix can land (liveness under fairness), and a fix that is never right halts at the bound (safety). Open question: does a merge-queue ejection count toward the card's attempt bound? It extends the attempt-bound models in tla-card-lifecycle-counters-and-waits.

Target: after v1.4

From: a Gemini dialog the owner shared, 2026-10-10

### Coordinator drift: a root brief and two metrics

Every escalation carries the root brief, with a test that holds it. Every card cites a release-scope or fixes item directly, never through its parent card, which closes scope laundering. Drift is measured three ways: the share of newly written cards that cite no item in the release-scope or fixes file (cards carry their release); the Jaccard overlap of non-trivial tokens between a card's brief and its cited scope item, warning below a ratio such as 15%; and the branching ratio, consumer cards per producer card per wave. The blind spots these close are scope laundering, semantic dilution and scope bloat.

Target: after v1.4

Since PR #499 START honours the STOP receipt the STOPPED friend reconcile writes when it retires a friend's working and read cards (internal/sprint/live.go LiveReturns, friend_return.go). The reconcile fires on seat.Unhooked, which nova-hook unhook sets by command: it is not evidence the friend's session stopped. A friend unhooked after a STOP while her session still works a card lets START pass and the primary be dealt again beside her; her stale finish is refused (the card is off the table, its generation stepped), so two processes can work one primary but neither corrupts it. tla/StopReturn.tla Retire assumes child = 0, which the code does not check on this path. Decide the evidence (a live set that no longer names the job, or an explicit cancel acknowledgement) and write the receipt only on it; extend the model so Retire is enabled only on that evidence, with a reversed witness.

### Swarm mode: the whole fleet and every friend go wide on one problem

A new mode beside the deal. Instead of many cards to many workers, one hard problem goes to every lane at once: every fleet member's lanes and every friend's width, each attacking the same problem independently. Coordination is shared across the message bus plus a few text files in a repo: a findings log (what each lane learned), a dead-ends list (what failed and why, so no lane repeats it), and a leaderboard of candidate heads with their gate results. The problem's tests, or an outside judge, rank the candidates; the first head that passes every gate wins, or the best one at a deadline. Design questions for the card: diversity across lanes (different models, tiers, prompts and starting points, so lanes are not copies); how much each lane reads of the shared files, and when (sharing too early collapses diversity, too late wastes work); a budget and a stop rule (a token cap, a wall clock, and stopping once a winner lands); merging partial results from several lanes; and fairness of the bus under many writers. It is a state machine (lanes, candidates, judging, stop), so its TLA+ model comes first. Predicated on nova-tools v1.7 rename-nova-swarm-to-nova-worker, which frees the name: this mode is nova-swarm.

Why it waits: Some problems are worth many independent attempts at once: hard bugs, R&D and frontier cards. Today the sprint can only split work, not converge many minds on one problem.

Target: v1.7

### Composite verbs: one call does each coordinator act, end to end

Learned from Hermes Agent's programmatic tool calling, which collapses a multi-step pipeline into one inference call. Each coordinator act that today takes 3 to 6 verbs, with traps on the way, becomes one deterministic verb that does the whole act and prints only what to act on. Measured on 2026-10-16: (1) stuck: list every card that is not moving but could be, and why: waiting with every need landed, held by a judgment, or merging but not queued. This is today's tools/stuck-cards-review.sh made a verb. (2) refinish-same-head: re-finish a card whose only fault was the bench or the gate, checking first that the head merges onto the base. (3) fix-missing-base: add a recut card's missing REPO or BASE line in any column (return, brief --keep-head, accept). (4) resolve-bound: clear a misclassified attempt bound (release, then an in-place brief with a dated carry line). (5) accept-on-read: record a cold read with its evidence file, choosing --heavy or --read-ok itself. Each verb has --dry-run, refuses by name with the one next command, and is tested on a real store, including every refusal. Glenn, 2026-10-16: skills are non-deterministic, so lessons become deterministic verbs and checks, never prose skills the agent must remember to apply.

Why it waits: Every manual multi-verb act today cost tokens and hit at least one refusal that needed another verb first; one deterministic verb per act removes both.

Target: v1.7

From: Glenn, live, 2026-10-16, on the Hermes Agent review: '#2 is great idea for v1.7' and 'skills are fine, but remember, skills are non-deterministic'

### Every resolved judgment becomes a recorded lesson, and repeated lessons become verbs or checks

Learned from Hermes Agent's skill loop (the agent writes a skill after solving something and improves it with use), but made deterministic. Glenn, 2026-10-16: skills are non-deterministic. The machine records every resolved judgment as data: the judgment kind, the cause the coordinator named, the verbs that fixed it, and how long the card was stuck. When a cause repeats past a threshold, the machine raises a named judgment proposing the fix as code: a composite verb (composite-verbs-one-call-per-coordinator-act), a refusal that names the next command, or a check that stops the cause at its source, so a hulk-style bench fault or a recut card with no BASE line is caught before it strands cards. A lesson never lives only as prose for an agent to remember. Today's examples, to seed it: a bench gate on the wrong Go, a misclassified attempt bound, a recut card missing REPO and BASE lines blocking a whole stream's batch, a false empty-commit on a no-ff merge over a carried head, soft land-after deps on file overlap, and stale GATE-NEEDS judgments after members gained facts.

Why it waits: The coordinator fixed the same few causes by hand many times today; recording them as data and turning repeats into code makes the fix permanent and deterministic.

Target: v1.7

### Card lint locks in the coordinator's lessons: 16 new rules from 30 hours of failed cards

From the coaching analysis of 408 failed events, 2026-10-16 (~/rowan-working/coaching/2026-10-16.md, section 4). 78 events, plus 57 machine PATHS widenings and 156 brief-replaced bounces, were the brief's fault, not the worker's. Each lesson becomes a deterministic rule at add, brief, recut and --widen, refusing with the one next command: L1 generated-outputs-in-paths (needs a per-repo map of which emitter writes which generated files); L2 registry-rows-in-paths (extends paths-cover-registry to make/<lang>.mk, make/negative-controls.json, tablenames, tla CASES/RUNS/RUNS-HISTORY, tools/agentsmap/catalog.go); L3 pinned-digest-in-paths; L4 changed-rule-pins-in-paths (tests and docs that pin the rule being changed); L5 every-brief-names-repo-and-base; L6 needs-are-header-lines-and-live (a named dependency is a DEPENDS-ON or LAND-AFTER line naming a live card); L7 overlap-on-the-table-needs-an-order; L8 donewhen-runs-at-base (every target, script, driver, TLA module, TLC group and sibling exists at BASE or inside PATHS/NEW); L9 siblings-named; L10 host-words-need-gate-needs; L11 staged-job-or-machine-only; L12 roadmap-flip-needs-row-coverage; L13 measure-card-names-its-driver (and refuses a hand-made board); L14 form-has-a-checker (needs a review-checker command); L15 pin-only-to-an-up-friend; L16 tier-floor-by-size (only ever raises a tier). Also from today: BASE must be a stream branch, never another card's branch, since a card that landed onto a card branch never reached its stream (rocketnet-message-objects-and-c-api). Every rule is tested on a real store, including each refusal, and replayed against today's failed cards to show it would have caught them.

Why it waits: Lessons that live in prose are forgotten; skills are non-deterministic (Glenn, same day). A lint rule refuses the bad card before it costs an attempt.

Target: v1.7

From: the coordinator, 2026-10-16

### One app starts at login and runs every nova service on the machine, configured from the friend list, never a launch agent per friend or job

After the 2026-10-16 reboot the studio had 45 files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents and more in /Library/LaunchDaemons, a plist for each friend hook (aurora, emma, johnny, stella), each friend runner, each loop, the dashboards, the redis instances and the sprint server. 19 were stale: editor backups, before-* and moved-to-* copies, a duplicate Stella hook, and sprint-table-live, which had crash-looped 23,923 times on a retired verb. Two more broke on the reboot because their paths pointed at a versioned Homebrew Cellar node and at /tmp. Each friend added, moved or retired meant a hand-written plist, and nothing removed the old one. The fix is one supervisor, installed as the only nova launch agent on a machine (plus one daemon only where root is needed, such as the CI runners). It reads which friends live on this machine, their harness, dirs and sessions from nova-config, and the machine's roles (store, sprint server, dashboard, hook-serve, loops) from the same config. It starts each child, restarts it with backoff, writes one log per child, and reports per-child state so nova-doctor shows a crash loop at once. Adding or moving a friend is a config change: the supervisor starts or stops her children, and a retired job disappears because config is the only source. It refuses a path under /tmp or a versioned Cellar path, and nova-doctor flags any other nova plist on the machine as a stray. The supervisor's states (absent, starting, running, backing-off, stopped, removed) get a TLA+ model before code, and unit tests use a fake clock and a fake process starter. Covers nova-tools binaries too (nova-hook, nova-friend, nova-swarm loops, nova-secrets exec wrappers), and the fleet's ansible plays install only the supervisor.

Why it waits: A launch agent per friend and per job grew to dozens of plists that nobody removed, and stale ones broke things and loaded the machine (Glenn, 2026-10-16).

Target: v1.7

From: Glenn, live, 2026-10-16: 'consolidate all these things into one app that starts at startup and has configuration according to friends, not an app per-friend'

### nova-sprint log honours --max and names the rest

Repository mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint. Extends nova-sprint log (cmd/nova-sprint/log.go), never a second mechanism. Problem: `nova-sprint log --since 1h --max 5` printed 2,985 entries, ending `LOG OK lines=2985 of=127415` (854 KB). log.go never reads c.max, and log.go:120 prints every line. Smallest fix: honour --max with a default of 20, end a cut list with `MORE kind=log shown=<n> total=<t> run: nova-sprint log <same filters> --max 0`, and add --grep and --kind later if needed. The help text is corrected by the v1.4.x text fix (the store-verbs --max paragraph now says log does not cap yet); this is the behaviour, and the fix reverses that paragraph when it lands. Tool: nova-sprint log. Tests are unit tests: no real time, no sockets, no network.

Why it waits: A bounded look at the log cost 854 KB because --max is parsed and ignored.

### CI pause, part 1 of 3 (nova-sprint): fleet quiet --ci pauses a machine's runners for a bounded window, with the model

Repository mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint, tier heavy. Extends fleet quiet (cmd/nova-sprint/fleetquiet.go; rule internal/sprint/fleet_quiet.go: Quiet, quietPlan, quietEnds, QuietLines), never a second mechanism: Quiet gains ci, FleetReq (internal/sprint/steps_work.go) carries it, the queue answer gains ci_pause (cmd/nova-sprint/view.go), fleet beat gains --runners (cmd/nova-sprint/fleet.go, stored in internal/sprint/presence.go), where gains the ci cell (cmd/nova-sprint/reads.go); docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section fleet-quiet-machine-b.w7 and docs/CLI.md follow. THE MODEL, written first: tla/RunnerPause.tla (clock, pause, per runner state, job, interrupted; actions Tick, SetPause with until <= clock + Cap, EndPause, JobStart, JobEnd, GateStep, and RaceAssign, the accepted race of a job assigned between the gate's read and its SIGINT). Properties NeverSignalBusy, BoundedPause, PausedOnlyWhilePaused and the liveness ResumesAfterDeadline. Three reversed witnesses: MCRunnerPauseBrokenKillBusy fails NeverSignalBusy, MCRunnerPauseBrokenNoExpiry fails ResumesAfterDeadline, MCRunnerPauseBrokenNoCap fails BoundedPause; group runnerpause in tla/CASES.tsv, TLC on a Linux bench, records merged with tlacheck merge --keep. Tests: internal/sprint TestFleetQuietCIPausesAndEndsAtItsTime, cmd/nova-sprint TestFleetQuietCIVerbQueueBeatAndWhere. THE CONTRACT, shared by the three CI-pause entries (ci-pause-sprint-record, ci-pause-runner-gate, ci-pause-member-carrier): (1) Record: fleet quiet <m> (--for|--until) --reason <text> --ci sets the member's quiet with ci true; the deal effect is the quiet's as today; a CI quiet more than 24h from now is refused, nothing written, naming the cap (CIQuietMost); --end and the tick's quietEnds end the CI pause with the quiet; the QUIET line of a CI quiet ends '; CI paused'. (2) Carrier: queue --as <m> --json carries ci_pause {until RFC3339 UTC, until_unix, reason} while the asking member's CI quiet is active, and no ci_pause key otherwise. (3) Pause file: the member writes it atomically (temp file in the same directory, then rename) as {until, until_unix, set_unix, reason} while ci_pause is present and removes it when absent; its path is the runner unit's NOVA_CI_PAUSE_FILE: linux the seat's $HOME/nova-bench/runners/ci-pause.json, darwin /Users/Shared/nova-runners/ci-pause.json (mode 2775, group staff: the darwin runner seat is a separate account). (4) Gate, per runner, FAIL OPEN: a pause is active iff the file parses, now < until_unix and until_unix <= set_unix + 86400; absent, unreadable, past or over the cap is no pause, CI on, so a dead sprint or member can never leave CI off. States: enabled -> draining (pause active, the runner's Runner.Worker is running a job) -> paused (child stopped by SIGINT) -> enabled (pause not active: child started again); enabled goes straight to paused when idle; draining goes back to enabled with no signal when the pause lifts first. DRAIN, NEVER KILL: the gate never signals a child whose Runner.Worker is running. It polls every NOVA_GATE_EVERY seconds (default 15). (5) Gate report: <pause dir>/state/<runner name>.json {state, at_unix} on each change. (6) Beat and view: the member sends fleet beat <m> --runners enabled=<n>,draining=<n>,paused=<n>,unmanaged=<n> (unmanaged: a Runner.Listener with no state file, e.g. one started from a shell outside its unit) only when the installed fleet beat -h lists --runners; the beat stores the counts beside no_room and refuses a malformed word naming the form; where and where --all show one cell per fleet member: ci=on, ci=paused until <time>, ci=draining <n>, ci=unmanaged <n> (the remedy is a converge of that host's runners), ci=- with no counts; where --json carries the same. Unit tests use no real time (clocks start at 1000 seconds), no sockets, no network: fakes for the store, the server, the process table and the files; real runner control is functional-tier only, and converging the fleet stays the coordinator's act.

Why it waits: fleet quiet and fleet hold stop sprint deals only; nothing pauses a machine's GitHub Actions runners, and a quiet window on amd-1 on 2026-10-16 was made by stopping its runners by hand. A pause must let running jobs finish, can never stay on past its deadline, and shows in the sprint's views.

Target: v1.7

From: Glenn, live, 2026-10-16: 'Please add a card so you can disable CI from running on machines as needed. 1.7'

### ROADMAP.md is feature tables with check marks and crosses, like schema's

Every repository's roadmap renders as one section per area and one table of user-recognisable features with done and remaining cells and a complete percentage row, evidence for each done cell kept in the data, as schema's ROADMAP.md does. pkg/roadmap (nova-tools) gains feature and evidence records and the table render; nova-work roadmap verbs and nova-sprint pick it up with the next nova-tools bump, so both repos switch together. Locked out of v1.4.8 because the renderer ships inside nova-work and nova-sprint.

Target: v1.7

From: the owner, 2026-10-17: the standard format for all roadmaps, including nova tools and nova sprint

### One roadmap format for every repository, one renderer, and defer writes it

Every repository (nova-sprint, nova-tools, schema, rocketnet, ideas and the rest) keeps its roadmap in one form, and one renderer produces the feature-table ROADMAP.md (generated check marks and crosses, as schema's is; see roadmap-as-feature-tables). nova-sprint defer, and anything else that writes a roadmap, writes that one form. Existing roadmaps are migrated once. Problem, two forms today: nova-sprint keeps docs/roadmap.sexp as `(roadmap "v1" ...)` rendered by `go tool roadmap` (make roadmap); mas-bandwidth/schema keeps its roadmap as `(:schema 1 :root ... :nodes (...))` rendered to ROADMAP.md by tools/roadmap/render.lisp. nova-sprint defer writes a deferred card's brief into a checkout's docs/roadmap.sexp, but only in the sprint's own form, so on schema it refused: `does not decode: roadmap: top: want one (roadmap "v1" ...) form`, and the schema non-Go streams had to be recorded by hand. Smallest fix: choose the one form with the owner, make the single renderer read it, make defer and every writer emit it, and migrate each existing roadmap once with a check that the rendered ROADMAP.md is unchanged in content. Tools: nova-sprint defer, the roadmap renderer (go tool roadmap), schema tools/roadmap/render.lisp. Tests are unit tests: no real time, no sockets, no network.

Why it waits: Two roadmap forms mean defer cannot write to schema, and records are made by hand.

Target: v1.7

From: the owner, 2026-10-17: 'please log this for v1.7. We should have only one roadmap format.'

### The nightly TLC run is red on the same models every night

tla/tlc.yml's nightly (04:17 UTC) has failed on main every night since 2026-10-15 on the same cases: dirtytick-goals, dirtytick-handback-live-lapse, dirtytick-small, landpass, level, serverswitch, stopreturn (and sprintrules, sprinttables on 10-17). The nightly gates nothing, so nobody looked; on 2026-10-18 it ran on the v1.6.0 release commit and its red check runs refused the cut (nova-update release cut reads every check run on the commit), which is how it was found. Find whether each case is a model that no longer fits the runner's time, a stale fingerprint, or a real counterexample; fix each or move it to the certification tier by name; and make the nightly's red reach the coordinator's inbox. Target v1.7.

Why it waits: a red nobody reads is a rule nobody has (tla/README.md); and a release cut should never be the first reader of a nightly

### A friend row takes its ready queue by itself

A friend row whose seat is live takes every card dealt to its ready queue at once, up to its width, without any session deciding; the take starts the worker the row's harness configures, at a model no lower than the card's tier (heavy and frontier go to the row's strongest model). A card the row cannot run is refused back to the deal with a judgment naming why, never left sitting ready. Where shows the dealt-to-taken latency per row; a ready card untaken past 60 s on a live row with free width raises one judgment. The model (FriendReadyTake) gains the invariant that a live row with free width holds no ready card past one tick, with a reversed witness. Tests run on the in-memory twin with time as an argument. The full brief is kept at working/tmp/v15cards/a-friend-row-takes-its-ready-queue-by-itself.md. Source: Glenn 2026-10-16 ~00:35Z: "Add a card to v1.5 to setup something so you take cards in ready queue automatically. that is the disgn and the intent."

Why it waits: Cards sat in a friend row's ready queue for long stretches on 2026-10-15 because taking waited for a dispatcher session to decide.

Target: v1.5

From: Glenn, 2026-10-16 ~00:35Z

### A friend's dispatcher follows its row width by itself

The width in nova-config is the one true source for how many workers a friend's dispatcher runs. Today the coordinator changes `nova-config friend set <f> --width N` and then has to message the friend to resize her dispatcher child; that second step goes away. friend-sync already writes the width to the friend's row. Either the friend's hook pushes a width-changed notice, or the dispatcher reads the row width (from `nova-sprint friend cards <f>` or a `friend width` verb) on every loop and runs up to that many workers, with reads at half a slot. Nobody tells the friend. Tests: a unit test with no real time, where changing the configured width changes the dispatcher's concurrency on its next loop; and a functional test on a real store, where shrinking the width never kills a running worker and only stops new takes. The width/take loop is a state machine, so the TLA+ module is extended (FriendReadyTake) or a new one added: the width the dispatcher runs to equals the row width within one loop, and a shrink never terminates a running worker, each with a reversed witness. Related: the v1.5 entry a-friend-row-takes-its-ready-queue-by-itself (#431). Source: Glenn 2026-10-16: "Each friend should *automatically* update their dispatcher when their width changes in nova-config. It should not be a second step."

Why it waits: Changing a friend's width needed a second step, a message to the friend, so the dispatcher could run at the old width until someone remembered.

Target: v1.5

From: Glenn, 2026-10-16

### The friend deal rotates over equally idle friends

preferredFriend (internal/sprint/friend_deal.go) picks the friend with the most idle lanes, then the most free room, then the first by name, so a tie always goes to the same friend. A persisted friend_deal_index on the fleet table, kept like deal_index (round.go PropDealIndex), breaks the tie as ((index + 1) % n), so the first name never always wins. A unit test shows two equally idle friends alternate across ticks, and tla/WhoPreference.tla gains a fairness property: no eligible friend is starved while another is dealt two.

Why it waits: A new deal counter, held out of the 1.4.x point releases, which take only critical breakers.

Target: v1.5

From: Glenn, 2026-10-16: "Remember to do the ( index + 1 ) % n when dealing so you don't bias to the top." (scoped out of v1.4.4 by the freeze rule)

### A friend's card lanes run each card on the model of its tier

A friend's one-shot lane runs every card on the friend's one model, whatever the card's tier. The friend row names a model per tier it serves, and a lane launches each card, work or read, on the model of the card's tier, never below it (the rule of #432, a card is never worked or read below its tier).

Why it waits: A new row field and lane launch rule.

Target: v1.5

From: the coordinator, 2026-10-16

### A friend's own git identity on her nova-config row

friend stage sets the clone's identity from the friend row's git_identity, but the nova-config friend kind has no such field (the row's fields are tiers, roles, width, mode, config_dir, token_cap, streams, kinds, pronouns and session), so every friend delivery was refused until v1.4.5 fell back to the sprint row's git_identity. The friend kind gains git_identity (a migration, apply, and nova-config friend set --git_identity), each friend's identity set by the owner, and stage prefers it (identity=friend).

Why it waits: A schema migration on the fleet's configuration store, held out of the point release.

Target: v1.5
